body:
Can you look at #172 #180 #184 #186 and check if the code is meaningfully improved in the process?

@sepo-agent /answer

comments.body:
Yes. Across #172, #180, #184, and #186, the review -> fix-pr loop produced meaningful code improvements, not just style churn.

| PR | Meaningful improvement from the loop |
| --- | --- |
| #172 | Fixed review-provenance reliability: head capture now degrades instead of hard-gating review output, reviewer lanes still run if prepare fails, rubrics review is independent again, and marker parsing was tightened. See `capture-pr-head.ts`, `post-comment.ts`, and `agent-review.yml` at final head `adbb1dc`. |
| #180 | Fixed a real approval-authority bug: self-approval now blocks when the approval actor matches the PR author, which would otherwise fail or violate GitHub’s approval model. It also added missing success-path coverage. See `evaluateSelfApprovalActor`, `prepare-self-approve.ts`, and `resolve-self-approve.ts` at `e7d2724`. |
| #184 | Fixed orchestration correctness: terminal self-approval outcomes now hand back to the orchestrator, not only `REQUEST_CHANGES`. Without this, approved/blocked/failed child work could stop locally and fail to resume the parent. See `agent-self-approve.yml` and `resultStateFromTerminal` at `4062890`. |
| #186 | Fixed operational/idempotency edge cases: stop comments now only post after prepare produced an intended body, and self-approval upsert failures no longer fall back to creating duplicate marker comments. See `agent-self-approve.yml` and `post-response.ts` at `9a51528`. |

My read: **the loop materially improved safety, correctness, and reliability**, especially because these PRs touch privileged self-approval and orchestrated follow-up behavior. The strongest wins were catching an approval actor bug in #180 and a lost orchestrator handback path in #184. #186 was more edge-case hardening, but still meaningful because it preserves the idempotent status-comment contract.

title: Does the orchestrator review fix loop meaningfully improve the code?
